clue.text: Without opening mouth, are they pious holy men?

definitions.text: Without opening mouth, are they pious holy men?

parts.words: Without opening mouth, are they pious holy men?
parts.note: a trap is slang for a mouth; the clue pictures religious brothers bound by a rule of silence who never open theirs

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether silent men are truly devout.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAP is British slang for mouth ('shut your trap'), and these Cistercian monks keep a vow of silence, so they never open their traps.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of the strict Cistercian order of La Trappe are famous for keeping silence.

clue.text: Like agreements of 1 ac, I found in diplomacy?

indicators.note: found in says the letter I is discovered sitting inside the other word

parts.note: diplomacy means tact

explanation.surface: Asks whether the silent understandings of monks show up in statecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is 1 across, TRAPPISTS: their agreements are unspoken, since they keep silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent monks can only reach unspoken, implied understandings.

clue.text: Blacken Caesar's coin by itself

parts.note: the as was a small Roman coin, as Caesar would have used
per se is Latin for by itself

explanation.surface: Darkening a Roman coin on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to slander, to blacken someone's name.

clue.text: As husband, unusually heroic? Put in play by Shakespeare

definitions.text: As husband, unusually heroic? Put in play by Shakespeare

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the two words are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a husband was heroic and then appears in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges HEROIC and PUT; the whole clue describes the shrew-taming husband of The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the bold suitor who marries and tames Katherina in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Prize .someone ran up to get

parts.note: ran up suggests a runner-up, the person finishing second in a race, and what award goes to them

explanation.surface: An award someone sprinted uphill to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran up' plays on runner-up: second place in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up in Olympic-style events receives the award of second place.

clue.text: Deputize for one serving under captain in craft

definitions.text: one serving under captain in craft

explanation.surface: Standing in for a junior officer aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in for someone is to fill in as replacement; a subordinate officer serves beneath the commander of a vessel.

clue.text: Guardian disputes — no end of strike in sight

indicators.note: no says the following letter is to be dropped from the word

parts.note: disputes means argues

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of strike

explanation.surface: A protector quarrels while the end of a walkout stays out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of strike' removes E, the last letter of strike, from ARGUES. Argus was the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth set as watchman, always with something in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus of Greek myth, with a hundred eyes, was set as a watchman, so the name means a vigilant protector.

clue.text: Improvise new final section for 20

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the last five letters of 20 across, GARIBALDI

explanation.surface: Making up a fresh ending on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is 20 across, GARIBALDI, whose final section is BALDI; 'new' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking ad lib means extemporising, without a script.

clue.text: Awkward place to stick actor

parts.note: to stick is to gum
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Somewhere awkward to fasten a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up a gum tree' is a British idiom for being in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means stuck in a predicament.

clue.text: Putting together evil-sounding proposition

indicators.note: sounding says the words are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: evil means sin
a thesis is a proposition argued for

explanation.surface: Combining ideas into something that sounds wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthesis is the combining of parts into a whole.

clue.text: Money to provide the finishing touch, almost

indicators.note: almost says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: to cap it all is to provide a finishing touch

explanation.surface: Cash to round things off, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CAP IT ALL to drop its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is wealth, funds used to invest.

clue.text: Ring-leader of the B" crew

parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark, every crew member's job begins with B, and their captain rings a bell

explanation.surface: The chief of a second-rate gang.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark the crew (Baker, Butcher, Banker...) all start with B, led by the bell-ringing captain.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier who rings a bell is literally a leader with a ring, and Carroll's captain is the same figure.

clue.text: Foreigner you heard in Northern port

parts.note: a Turk serves as an example of a foreigner

indicators.note: heard says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: you is said like the letter U

explanation.surface: An outsider hears someone call in a harbour up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Turku is a seaport in south-west Finland.

clue.text: Site of castle in Northern Athens

explanation.surface: Where a fortress stands in a Greek city up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's capital has a famous castle on its rock, and was nicknamed the Athens of the North for its classical culture.

clue.text: Possibly in seven, is it? Number is more like this

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question about whether something fits into seven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is more numb, not a figure, despite 'seven' nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more numb means having less feeling, which is the state of lacking feeling.

clue.text: Unimpressive type can't cut these diamonds

definitions.text: Unimpressive type can't cut these diamonds

parts.words: Unimpressive type can't cut these diamonds
parts.note: an unimpressive person is said not to cut it, the idiom about making no impression, and these diamonds are slang gems

explanation.surface: A poor jeweller unable to cut certain stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone unimpressive 'cuts no ice', and the word is also slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Underworld slang calls diamonds by this word for their frozen glitter.

clue.text: Noticing nothing odd in disguise

indicators.note: odd says the letters are made strange, put out of order

parts.note: nothing is O, zero

explanation.surface: Spotting nothing strange about a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Going incognito means hiding one's identity.

clue.text: Roman sage includes us all

explanation.surface: A Latin wise man embraces everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin species name means wise man, and names the whole human race.

clue.text: Blessed, we hear, this sort of labour

definitions.text: Blessed, we hear, this sort of labour

parts.words: Blessed, we hear, this sort of labour
parts.note: Blessed are the peacemakers, so peace work is blessed, and that is heard as a kind of paid work

explanation.surface: Being told some kind of toil is holy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatitudes say 'Blessed are the peacemakers'; peace work sounds like work paid by the item.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecework is labour paid per item produced.

clue.text: Agreement to provide detailed references

explanation.surface: A deal to supply fuller citations.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony; an index of every place a word appears in a text is a reference work.

clue.text: Hurry up! Produce notes for medical treatment

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hurry means run
to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: Telling someone to hurry and bring the paperwork for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for the sick is the work of tending patients.

clue.text: Practical cat has a right to leave 6

indicators.note: to leave says those letters depart from the word

parts.note: 6 across, ARGUS

explanation.surface: A sensible cat is entitled to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Gus the Theatre Cat is one of T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Practical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Gus appears in T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.

clue.text: First-class degree for relatively old woman

parts.note: grand means first-class
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A top degree for a fairly elderly lady.
explanation.definitionFit: She is an old woman relative: a parent's mother.

clue.text: National leader of note — a scurrilous one

parts.note: G is a musical note
ribald means coarse, scurrilous
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A notable leader who is a foul-mouthed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi led the fight to unify Italy.

clue.text: Note what's right, using such intelligence

parts.note: B is a musical note
the saying 'right as rain' makes rain the thing that is right

explanation.surface: Writing down the correct answer, using one's wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's right' leans on the phrase 'as right as rain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is used for mental power or cleverness.

clue.text: Head for this antelope?

parts.note: putting head in place of the first letter of the animal's name gives a coastal promontory

explanation.surface: Asks for the head of an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap HEAD for the opening E of the animal and you get headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Staff upset my unassailable position on course

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a rod is a staff

explanation.surface: Staff knock over my position on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf matchplay a player is dormy when leading by as many holes as remain, so cannot lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer ahead by as many holes as are left cannot be beaten in that match.

clue.text: Perform action like Henry's tiger or ape

explanation.surface: Acting like Shakespeare's tiger, or a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry V the king urges his men to 'imitate the action of the tiger'.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's behaviour is to mimic it, as Henry V's soldiers were told to do the tiger.

clue.text: Midsummer, say, in German town?

parts.note: the middle of summer is the pair of letters M, and those two letters spelt out name a spa town

explanation.surface: Midsummer celebrations in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of 'summer' are two Ms, and the plural of the letter name M names Bad Ems, a German spa.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad Ems is a spa town in western Germany.

clue.text: Fitting like 1 ac

explanation.surface: Appropriate like the monks.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is 1 across, TRAPPISTS: monks belonging to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Properly arranged means suitable; monks are members of a religious brotherhood.

clue.text: Pipes stopped in the loft?

parts.note: pipes sound like plumbing frozen in an attic, but stops are knobs on a church instrument kept in a loft

explanation.surface: Plumbing blocked up in the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumbing in an attic is the false path; a church instrument has stops and pipes and sits in a gallery called a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: The church instrument has pipes, stops, and sits in a gallery named after it.

clue.text: Demand reply from midshipman in bar

parts.note: speak is the command demanding an answer
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's novel

explanation.surface: Ordering a junior naval officer to answer in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is Frederick Marryat's 1836 sea novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was an illicit drinking den during Prohibition.
